Adventuring Gear.oracle_text:
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, equipped creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn.
Equip {1} ({1}: Attach to target creature you control. Equip only as a sorcery.)

Band Together.oracle_text: Up to two target creatures you control each deal damage equal to their power to another target creature.

Canopy Baloth.oracle_text: Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, this creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn.

Dwynen's Elite.oracle_text: When this creature enters, if you control another Elf, create a 1/1 green Elf Warrior creature token.

Elvish Archdruid.oracle_text:
Other Elf creatures you control get +1/+1.
{T}: Add {G} for each Elf you control.

Elvish Rejuvenator.oracle_text: When this creature enters, look at the top five cards of your library. You may put a land card from among them onto the battlefield tapped. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.

Elvish Warmaster.oracle_text:
Whenever one or more other Elves you control enter, create a 1/1 green Elf Warrior creature token. This ability triggers only once each turn.
{5}{G}{G}: Elves you control get +2/+2 and gain deathtouch until end of turn.

Garruk's Harbinger.oracle_text:
Hexproof from black
Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player or planeswalker, look at that many cards from the top of your library. You may reveal a creature card or Garruk planeswalker card from among them and put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.

Garruk, Unleashed.oracle_text:
+1: Up to one target creature gets +3/+3 and gains trample until end of turn.
−2: Create a 3/3 green Beast creature token. Then if an opponent controls more creatures than you, put a loyalty counter on Garruk.
−7: You get an emblem with "At the beginning of your end step, you may search your library for a creature card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle."

Hunter's Insight.oracle_text: Choose target creature you control. Whenever that creature deals combat damage to a player or planeswalker this turn, draw that many cards.

Oashra Cultivator.oracle_text: {2}{G}, {T}, Sacrifice this creature: Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

Primeval Herald.oracle_text:
Trample (This creature can deal excess combat damage to the player or planeswalker it's attacking.)
Whenever this creature enters or attacks, you may search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

Rampaging Baloths.oracle_text:
Trample
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, create a 4/4 green Beast creature token.

Rampaging Growth.oracle_text: Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle. Until end of turn, that land becomes a 4/3 Insect creature with reach and haste. It's still a land.

Reclamation Sage.oracle_text: When this creature enters, you may destroy target artifact or enchantment.

Roots of Wisdom.oracle_text: Mill three cards, then return a land card or Elf card from your graveyard to your hand. If you can't, draw a card. (To mill a card, put the top card of your library into your graveyard.)

Silhana Wayfinder.oracle_text: When this creature enters, look at the top four cards of your library. You may reveal a creature or land card from among them and put it on top of your library. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.

Skyway Sniper.oracle_text:
Reach (This creature can block creatures with flying.)
{2}{G}: This creature deals 1 damage to target creature with flying.

Snapping Gnarlid.oracle_text: Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.

Thriving Grove.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped. As it enters, choose a color other than green.
{T}: Add {G} or one mana of the chosen color.

Titanic Growth.oracle_text: Target creature gets +4/+4 until end of turn.

Wildheart Invoker.oracle_text: {8}: Target creature gets +5/+5 and gains trample until end of turn. (It can deal excess combat damage to the player or planeswalker it's attacking.)

Okay, opponent played Garruk's Harbinger — a 4/3 with hexproof from black that draws cards on combat damage. That's a serious threat! I need to deal with it.

They blocked with Oashra Cultivator (Warmaster dealt 2, Cultivator has 3 toughness so it survived). Wait, no — looking at the life totals, opponent is still at 20, so they must have blocked. And Warmaster is still alive, so the 0/3 blocked and Warmaster dealt 2 damage to it (it survived since 3 toughness).

Now, my plan for this turn:
- I have 4 untapped lands
- Dwynen's Elite (1G) is an Elf that makes a token since I control another Elf → triggers Warmaster too!
- Skyway Sniper (G) is another Elf with reach
- I could cast both for 3 mana total, getting 2 Warmaster triggers (2 more tokens)

That gives me a wide board. Then I can use Band Together next turn to deal with Harbinger if needed. Or I could hold up Titanic Growth for a combat trick.

Let me think about Harbinger — it's 4/3 and attacks next turn. I need to be able to block or remove it. Band Together with 2 creatures dealing their power could handle it.

Best line: Cast Dwynen's Elite (1G) → triggers Warmaster (token), Dwynen's Elite ETB (token). Then cast Skyway Sniper (G) → triggers Warmaster again (another token). That's 3 mana, I still have 1 left for Elven Bow if I want. But Skyway Sniper has reach so it can block flyers.

Actually, let me cast Dwynen's Elite first, then Skyway Sniper. That gives me tons of bodies.

Opponent can block with Cultivator 0/3 only (Beast is sick). I can send Dwynen's Elite + 1 token at Garruk (3 damage = kills it), and the rest at face (4 damage to opponent, going to 12).

Let me cast Warmaster first for the token value, then attack.

Should I block the Beast (3/3) or the Forest-Insect (4/3)?

- Block Beast 3/3: Warmaster deals 2 to Beast (doesn't kill it), Beast deals 3 to Warmaster (kills it). I take 4 from the Insect.
- Block Forest-Insect 4/3: Warmaster deals 2 to Insect (doesn't kill it), Insect deals 4 to Warmaster (kills it). I take 3 from Beast.

Either way Warmaster dies since both attackers have more than 2 toughness. The Forest-Insect is temporary (goes back to being a land at end of turn), so I should block the Beast 3/3 since it's permanent. If I block Beast, I save 3 life (take 4 instead of 7). If I block Insect, I save 4 life (take 3 instead of 7).

Actually the math: blocking saves me 0 damage if I don't kill the creature. It just redirects the damage. I take total = unblocked damage.

- Block Beast: Take 4 from Insect (Beast's damage goes to Warmaster, not me). Total: 4 damage.  
- Block Insect: Take 3 from Beast. Total: 3 damage.
- No block: Take 7 damage.

So blocking the Insect saves more life (take 3 vs 4). But Warmaster is my best remaining creature and a key engine piece. Losing it is terrible.

Hmm, but taking 7 to 13 is still okay. I'm ahead on board with 7 creatures. The Insect goes away at end of turn. Warmaster will generate tons of value if it survives.

I should NOT block. Preserve Warmaster. Take the 7, go to 13. Next turn Warmaster can create tokens when I play elves.

llmEvents.reasoning:
Turn 7! Drew Reclamation Sage (2/1 for 2G, destroys an artifact/enchantment on ETB). 13 life vs 16, I need to be aggressive.

My options:
1. **Reclamation Sage (2G)** - It's an Elf! Triggers Warmaster to create a token. Can destroy their Adventuring Gear. 2/1 body.
2. **Wildheart Invoker (2GG)** - Big 4/3, but not an Elf so no Warmaster trigger. Costs all 4 mana.
3. **Band Together (2G)** - Removal spell. Could kill the Beast token (pick 2 creatures dealing power to it).
4. **Elven Bow** - Create a 1/1 Elf token (2 mana) or equip.

The best play is Reclamation Sage:
- Triggers Warmaster → creates an Elf Warrior token
- Destroys Adventuring Gear (eliminates landfall pump threat)
- Leaves 1 mana open for Elven Bow activation? No, Bow costs 2 to create token or 3 to equip.

With 4 lands: Rec Sage costs 3, leaving 1 mana. Not enough for anything else.

Or I could play Wildheart Invoker (4/3) for all 4 mana — it's a much bigger body for attacking. But no synergy with Warmaster.

Actually, Rec Sage + Warmaster token = 2 new creatures (Rec Sage 2/1 + token 1/1). That's +3 power added. Wildheart Invoker = +4 power but only 1 body.

I think Reclamation Sage is better: removes Adventuring Gear (their only equipment), triggers Warmaster, and it's a solid Elf for the team. Let me play it.

- Block Beast 3/3 with Elf Token (1/1): Token dies, Beast takes 1 damage (survives at 3/2), I take 0. Lose a 1/1.
- Double block with both: Both die, Beast takes 3 damage and dies! That removes the Beast permanently.

Wait, Beast is 3/3. Rec Sage (2/1) + Token (1/1) = 3 power total. Beast deals 3 damage — I assign 2 to Sage (killing it) and 1 to Token (killing it). Both blockers die. Beast takes 3 damage total, which kills it.

Let's double block!

llmEvents.reasoning:
Beast is dead! Both my blockers killed it. Excellent trade. I lost an Elf token and Rec Sage (which already did its job) to remove their biggest recurring threat.

Turn 8! Drew a Forest. I'm at 13 life, they're at 11. I have 6 creatures, they just have Canopy Baloth 4/3 and Oashra Cultivator 0/3.

My board: 3 Elf tokens (1/1), Rejuvenator (1/1), Warmaster (2/2), Skyway Sniper (1/2) = 7 power
With 4 lands + Forest to play = 5 lands.

Options:
1. Play Forest → Cast Wildheart Invoker (2GG) = 4/3 body. 5 mana used, 0 left.
2. Play Forest → Cast Band Together (2G) to kill Canopy Baloth. Use 2 creatures to deal power to it. Need 4 damage to kill 4/3 Baloth. Warmaster (2) + Rec Sage... Sage is dead. Warmaster (2) + Skyway Sniper (1) = 3. Not enough! Warmaster (2) + Rejuvenator (1) = 3. Also not enough. I need 4 power combined to kill Baloth with Band Together and I can't get it.

Actually, if I play Wildheart Invoker (4/3) first, then I could use Band Together with Invoker (4) + anything to kill Baloth, but I wouldn't have mana for both.

Best plan: Play Forest, play Wildheart Invoker (4/3). Attack with everything. They can only block with Cultivator (0/3).

That gives me: 3 tokens (3) + Rejuvenator (1) + Warmaster (2) + Sniper (1) = 7 power attacking. Invoker is sick. They block 1 with Cultivator, 6+ gets through. They go from 11 to 5 or lower!

Wait, but Canopy Baloth can also block. It's marked as "sick" — was it just played? Yes, they played it turn 7. It entered tapped... no, sick means summoning sickness. By turn 8 it should... wait, it still says sick. Let me check.

They played it last turn (their turn 7) so it would have summoning sickness during their turn but should be able to block on MY turn 8. "Sick" might just be the display. Creatures can always block even with summoning sickness.

So blockers: Canopy Baloth 4/3 + Oashra Cultivator 0/3. That's two blockers. If Baloth blocks Warmaster (2/2), Warmaster dies and Baloth survives. Bad. If they block a token, Baloth kills it.

Hmm, with Band Together I could kill the Baloth before combat. Forest → 5 lands. Band Together costs 2G. I need 2 creatures to deal ≥4 damage. Warmaster (2) + any 1/1 = 3. Not enough for 4. Warmaster (2) + Sniper (1) = 3. Still short.

But wait — if I equip Elven Bow to something first? Elven Bow equips for {1}{G}. If I equip to Warmaster, it becomes 3/3. Then Band Together with Warmaster (3) + anything (1) = 4 damage, kills Baloth!

- If they double block, they kill 2 creatures but I still push through some damage.
- If Baloth blocks Sniper (1/2), Sniper dies. Cultivator blocks a token. 3 damage through. Opponent goes to 8.
- If Baloth blocks a token, token dies. Cultivator blocks another. 3 damage through (Sniper + Rejuvenator + 1 token). Same result.

Actually, they'll likely put Baloth on something and Cultivator on something. Max 2 blocked, so 3 creatures get through = 3 damage minimum. Opponent goes from 11 to 8.

Or I could send Warmaster too for 7 power total. They block 2, 5 gets through. But risking Warmaster to Baloth...

If Baloth blocks Warmaster: Warmaster (2) doesn't kill Baloth (3 toughness). Baloth (4) kills Warmaster. Terrible.

Keep Warmaster back. Send the other 5.

ELVISH ARCHDRUID! This is an INCREDIBLE draw! 2/2 for 1GG — gives all other Elves +1/+1, AND taps for G per Elf you control. With 7 Elves, that's +7 mana!

Let me think about sequencing:

**Option A: Band Together first, then Archdruid**
- Band Together (2G, 3 mana): Invoker (4) + Warmaster (2) = 6 damage → kills Rampaging Baloths 6/6
- Then Archdruid (1GG, 3 mana): 2 mana left... wait, I have 5 lands. 3 for Band Together, leaves 2. Archdruid costs 3 (1GG). Can't cast both!

Unless... Actually I have 5 untapped lands. Band Together = 3 mana. Archdruid = 3 mana. Total = 6. I only have 5 lands. Can't do both.

**Option B: Archdruid first**
- Cast Archdruid (1GG, 3 mana). All other Elves get +1/+1. Warmaster → 3/3, tokens → 2/2, Rejuvenator → 2/2, Invoker → 5/4 (wait, is Invoker an Elf? Yes! Elf Shaman!). 
- Warmaster triggers — creates another Elf token!
- Then Archdruid taps for G per Elf. I'll have tons of mana.
- Then Band Together: Invoker (5) + Warmaster (3) = 8 damage → kills Baloths easily!
- Or even just attack for massive damage!

Wait, Archdruid has summoning sickness so it can't tap for mana this turn. But the +1/+1 buff is static and immediate.

After Archdruid resolves + Warmaster token:
- Archdruid 2/2 (sick, doesn't buff itself)
- Warmaster 3/3 (+1/+1 from Archdruid)
- Invoker 5/4 (+1/+1)  
- Rejuvenator 2/2 (+1/+1)
- 5 Elf tokens at 2/2 (+1/+1)
- Total creatures: 9, attackable (non-sick): 7 (Warmaster 3, Invoker 5, Rejuvenator 2, 4 tokens at 2 each = 18 power)

Opponent has 8 life and 3 blockers (Baloths 6/6, Baloth 4/3, Cultivator 0/3). If they block 3 of my attackers, I still push through massive damage.

With 18 power attacking and them at 8 life... Even if they block optimally (Baloths blocks Invoker 5/4, Canopy Baloth blocks Warmaster 3/3, Cultivator blocks a 2/2 token), that's 3 creatures blocked. Remaining: Rejuvenator (2) + 3 tokens (2+2+2) = 8 damage. EXACTLY lethal!

But wait, Baloths has trample — it doesn't matter since it's blocking. And Warmaster (3/3) vs Canopy Baloth (4/3) — Warmaster deals 3 (kills Baloth), Baloth deals 4 (kills Warmaster). Invoker (5/4) vs Baloths (6/6) — Invoker deals 5 (not enough to kill 6/6), Baloths deals 6 (kills Invoker).

So unblocked: 4 creatures = 8 damage = LETHAL! If they block 3 and let 4 through, each at 2/2, that's 8 damage exactly lethal on 8 life!

But they could block differently — block smaller creatures to prevent some damage and take less. Let me think:
- They block Invoker (saves 5 damage), a token (saves 2), and another token (saves 2) = saves 9 damage. I deal 18-9 = 9. That's more than 8, still lethal!

Actually any 3 blocks from them saves at most... Let me think about it from the other side. 18 power attacking. They have 3 blockers. Maximum damage prevented = Invoker (5) + Warmaster (3) + token (2) = 10. I deal 8. Exactly lethal!

Or if they block the three biggest: Invoker (5) + Warmaster (3) + Rejuvenator (2) = 10 prevented. 18-10 = 8. STILL LETHAL!

Actually, they could block differently. If they block Invoker (5), one token (2), one token (2) = prevent 9. I deal 9. Overkill.

Best blocking for them: Block 3 creatures to maximize damage prevented. Top 3 attackers by power: Invoker (5), Warmaster (3), Rejuvenator/token (2). Block those = prevent 10. Remaining: 4 tokens × 2 = 8. EXACTLY 8 = LETHAL!

Wait, do they actually die? 8 damage against 8 life = exactly dead. YES!

So no matter how they block (with 3 blockers), I deal at least 8 damage which is exactly lethal! This is a guaranteed win!

Let me play Archdruid first.

annotations.description: Passed with 1 untapped Forest and Elven Bow as the only castable spell. The mana would go completely unused. Even without paying the {2} kicker, having the equipment on the battlefield is pure upside - it can be equipped later for +1/+2 and reach.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, wasting 1 mana with no other possible plays
annotations.betterLine: Cast Elven Bow for {G} (declining the {2} kicker) to put the equipment on the battlefield for free. It can be equipped to a creature later for meaningful stats and reach.

annotations.description: Passed with 1 untapped mana and the only available action being to equip Adventuring Gear to Oashra Cultivator. Equipping for free (mana that would otherwise be wasted) would set up landfall triggers for next turn when they play Forest or Thriving Grove from hand, turning the 0/3 into a 2/5 that could block the opponent's Elvish Warmaster or other threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, wasting 1 mana and missing the opportunity to equip Adventuring Gear.
annotations.betterLine: Equip Adventuring Gear to Oashra Cultivator for {1}, setting up landfall value for the following turn at no real cost.

annotations.description: Oashra Cultivator (0/3) could block the attacking Elvish Warmaster (2/2) and survive, preventing 2 damage for free. There's no downside to blocking here since the Cultivator has 3 toughness.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not block, taking 2 damage from Elvish Warmaster.
annotations.betterLine: Block Elvish Warmaster with Oashra Cultivator. The 0/3 survives combat against a 2/2, saving 2 life at no cost.

annotations.description: Passed with 3 untapped lands and nothing else to do, wasting the opportunity to sacrifice Oashra Cultivator for ramp. Activating it now would provide 5 mana next turn, enabling a turn-7 Garruk, Unleashed alongside a land drop, rather than having to wait. The 0/3 body provides minimal value as a blocker against the opponent's growing elf army.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using any mana, doing nothing this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Oashra Cultivator ({2}{G}, tap, sacrifice) to search for a basic land, ramping to 5 mana next turn to enable casting Garruk, Unleashed or Canopy Baloth + equip Adventuring Gear.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Elven Bow with the only remaining untapped mana when no other spells in hand could be cast for just {G}. The Bow would enter unattached (can't pay {2} for the token), but would be on the battlefield ready to equip later, providing +1/+2 and reach to any creature. Since Band Together and Titanic Growth both require more than 1 mana, there's no reason to hold up the green mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, wasting 1 available green mana with no instant-speed plays possible.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Elven Bow for {G} to get it onto the battlefield for future equipping. No combat tricks are castable with just 1 mana anyway, so there's no bluffing or reactive value in holding it open.

annotations.description: GPT53C Teach passed priority in postcombat main phase with an unplayed Thriving Grove in hand and a land drop remaining. Playing the land would have given them 4 mana sources next turn (important for casting Garruk, Unleashed next turn which costs 2GG, or Canopy Baloth). Additionally, playing the land would trigger Adventuring Gear's landfall if equipped to a creature, though currently nothing is equipped. More importantly, the extra mana is pure upside - there's no reason not to play the Thriving Grove.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn without playing Thriving Grove.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Grove (choosing no additional color needed since the deck appears mono-green), giving access to 4 mana next turn to cast Garruk, Unleashed or Canopy Baloth.

annotations.description: GPT53C Teach declined to attack with Garruk's Harbinger (4/3) when the opponent had very limited blocking options (mostly summoning sick 1/1s and a 2/2). More critically, they had Hunter's Insight in hand with exactly 3 mana available - attacking and casting Hunter's Insight on an unblocked Harbinger would draw 4 cards AND trigger Harbinger's ability to find a creature. Even if blocked by the 2/2 Dwynen's Elite, the Harbinger survives and kills the blocker. This was a massive missed opportunity for card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Garruk's Harbinger, then if unblocked cast Hunter's Insight on it to draw 4 cards and trigger Harbinger's ability. Even without Hunter's Insight, the attack is profitable since the opponent's best blocker is a 2/2 that trades unfavorably with the 4/3.

annotations.description: All of the opponent's creatures are either tapped or have summoning sickness, meaning Garruk's Harbinger 4/3 is guaranteed to connect for combat damage. Casting Hunter's Insight targeting the Harbinger before attacks would draw 4 cards when it deals combat damage — an enormous card advantage swing in Limited. The player had exactly 3 untapped Forests to cast it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Hunter's Insight, missing a guaranteed 4-card draw.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Hunter's Insight targeting Garruk's Harbinger, then attack with it for an unblockable 4 damage and draw 4 cards.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with 3 untapped lands and Oashra Cultivator's sacrifice ability available. Activating it would ramp from 3 to 4 lands (getting a 4th land tapped), allowing 5 mana next turn with Thriving Grove from hand. This enables casting Garruk, Unleashed or Canopy Baloth alongside other plays sooner. Instead, the 0/3 Cultivator sits on board doing very little.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 3 untapped mana and no action taken.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Oashra Cultivator ({2}{G}, tap, sacrifice) to search for a basic land, ramping to 5 mana next turn (4 lands + Thriving Grove from hand), enabling powerful plays like Garruk, Unleashed plus additional spells.

annotations.description: Adventuring Gear's landfall trigger is on the stack, and the game is offering the option to equip it to a creature in response. Since the Gear isn't currently equipped to anything, the +2/+2 landfall trigger will resolve doing nothing. By equipping to the 3/3 Beast token (or the Forest 4/3 creature), they would get +2/+2 on that creature for attacks this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting the landfall trigger resolve with no creature equipped, wasting the +2/+2 buff.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Adventuring Gear to equip it to the Beast Token 3/3 (making it effectively a 5/5) or the Forest 4/3 creature, then let the landfall trigger resolve to get the +2/+2 bonus for combat.

annotations.description: Cast Reclamation Sage to destroy an unequipped Adventuring Gear instead of deploying Wildheart Invoker, a much larger body (4/3 vs 2/1). The Gear was not currently equipped to anything and the opponent only had Oashra Cultivator as a potential equip target. Wildheart Invoker would have added significantly more board presence and pressure, which matters at 13 life needing to race.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Reclamation Sage to destroy Adventuring Gear
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wildheart Invoker (4/3) to maximize board presence and pressure. The Adventuring Gear could be dealt with later or may never become threatening given the opponent's limited board.

annotations.description: Blocked a 1/1 Elf Warrior token with Oashra Cultivator (0/3) instead of the 2/2 Elvish Warmaster. The Cultivator survives either block (3 toughness), but blocking the Warmaster would prevent 2 damage instead of 1, saving an extra point of life for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked a 1/1 Elf Warrior token with Oashra Cultivator 0/3
annotations.betterLine: Block Elvish Warmaster (2/2) with Oashra Cultivator (0/3) to prevent 2 damage instead of 1, since the Cultivator survives both blocks

annotations.description: Cast Canopy Baloth before playing the land and Snapping Gnarlid. The optimal line is to cast Snapping Gnarlid first (2 mana), then play Thriving Grove to trigger Snapping Gnarlid's landfall (+1/+1 making it a 3/3 for blocking), then cast Canopy Baloth with the remaining 4 mana. This gives a stronger defensive position at 11 life against the opponent's wide board of tokens.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Snapping Gnarlid first, then play Thriving Grove (triggering landfall on Gnarlid for a 3/3 blocker), then cast Canopy Baloth with remaining mana.

annotations.description: Held back Elvish Warmaster (2/2) from attacking when the only potential blocker is Oashra Cultivator (0/3), which can't kill any attacker. Canopy Baloth is summoning sick and can't block. Attacking with Warmaster would deal 2 additional damage (6 total through instead of 4), putting opponent to 5 instead of 7, with no meaningful risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with 5 creatures (5 power total) but held back Elvish Warmaster 2/2.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all 6 eligible creatures including Elvish Warmaster for 7 power total. Oashra Cultivator blocks one 1/1, dealing 6 damage to bring opponent from 11 to 5. The Warmaster faces no combat risk since Cultivator has 0 power.

annotations.description: GPT53C Teach used Canopy Baloth (4/3) to block a 1/1 Elf Warrior token instead of the Skyway Sniper (1/2), which is a more valuable creature due to its reach ability and activated flying-damage ability. Both die equally to the 4/3, so blocking the Sniper would have removed more value from the opponent's board.
annotations.actionTaken: Canopy Baloth blocked an Elf Warrior Token (1/1), killing it
annotations.betterLine: Block the Skyway Sniper (1/2) with Canopy Baloth to remove the more valuable creature, while still using Oashra Cultivator to absorb another point of damage

annotations.description: GPT53C Teach declined to attack with Canopy Baloth 4/3 when the opponent had only Elvish Warmaster 2/2 untapped as a blocker. At 8 life vs 13, they need to be aggressive. Attacking either deals 4 damage (putting opponent to 9) or trades very favorably with the 2/2 Warmaster. The opponent's wide board of elves will untap next turn, making this an important window to push damage. Additionally, Hunter's Insight in hand means future attacks with Canopy Baloth could generate massive card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Canopy Baloth. It either deals 4 damage or kills Elvish Warmaster (the opponent's most threatening creature due to its token-generating and pump abilities) while surviving as a 4/1.
